180	def _task_route_waypoints(origin: Position, task: Task) -> list[Position]:
181	    """Required remaining visit points after *origin* for *task*.
182	
183	    The same pickup/delivery rule is used by first-time assignment, rerouting
184	    after map changes (and the recovery/sidestep planning that shares it) and
185	    checkpoint validation, so the requirement lives in exactly one place:
186	
187	    * Goods not yet collected: the route must still reach the pickup and then
188	      the dropoff. Standing exactly on the pickup makes the pickup leg empty --
189	      the leg contributes no waypoint -- but planning never collects or
190	      completes anything by itself.
191	    * Goods already collected: the robot routes straight to the dropoff, even
192	      when the old pickup cell was closed afterwards; it is never sent back.
193	
194	    When *origin*, pickup and dropoff coincide the list is empty, which
195	    describes a feasible zero-step route and must not be confused with an
196	    unreachable one.
197	    """
198	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
199	    if not task.picked_up and origin != task.pickup:
200	        waypoints.append(task.pickup)
201	    last = waypoints[-1] if waypoints else origin
202	    if task.dropoff != last:
203	        waypoints.append(task.dropoff)
204	    return waypoints
205	
206	
207	def _plan_task_route(
208	    grid: GridMap, origin: Position, task: Task
209	) -> list[Position] | None:
210	    """Shortest feasible route through the task's required waypoints.
211	
212	    The returned list holds the cells after *origin* only, concatenating the
213	    deterministic shortest legs between consecutive required points. It is
214	    ``None`` when any required point cannot be reached, and an empty list for a
215	    feasible route with zero steps (origin already at the only destination).
216	    """
217	    route: list[Position] = []
218	    current = origin
219	    for waypoint in _task_route_waypoints(origin, task):
220	        try:
221	            leg = shortest_path(grid, current, waypoint)
222	        except ValueError:
223	            return None
224	        route.extend(leg)
225	        current = waypoint
226	    return route
227	
228	
229	class FleetSimulator:
230	    def __init__(self, grid: GridMap, robots: list[Robot], tasks: list[Task]) -> None:
231	        self.grid = grid
232	        # The map as built before any runtime edit; map-change history is
233	        # replayed against this baseline.
234	        self.base_grid = grid
235	        self.robots = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
236	        self.tasks = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
237	        self.tick = 0
238	        self.replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
239	        self.map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
240	        self._map_sequence = 0
241	        self.paused_tasks: set[str] = set()
242	        # Consecutive per-robot waits caused purely by other robots:
243	        # robot_id -> {"blocked_by": [robot_id, ...], "ticks": int}.
244	        self._traffic_waits: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
245	        positions = [robot.position for robot in robots]
246	        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
247	            raise ValueError("robots cannot share an initial position")
248	        if any(not grid.traversable(position) for position in positions):
249	            raise ValueError("robot starts outside traversable map space")
250	
251	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
252	    # Dynamic map edits
253	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
254	
255	    def modify_obstacles(
256	        self,
257	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
258	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
259	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
260	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
261	
262	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
263	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
264	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
265	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
266	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
267	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
268	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
269	
270	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
271	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
272	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
273	        distance is accumulated.
274	        """
275	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
276	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
277	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
278	        if conflict:
279	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
280	            raise ValueError(
281	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
282	            )
283	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
284	        for cell in add_cells:
285	            if cell in occupied:
286	                raise ValueError(
287	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
288	                )
289	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
290	
291	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
292	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
293	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
294	        seen: set[Position] = set()
295	        ordered: list[Position] = []
296	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
297	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
298	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
299	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
300	            if position in seen:
301	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
302	                continue
303	            seen.add(position)
304	            ordered.append(position)
305	        return ordered
306	
307	    def _apply_map_change(
308	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
309	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
310	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
311	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
312	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
313	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
314	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
315	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
316	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
317	
318	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
319	        # known to change the map.
320	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
321	        self._map_sequence += 1
322	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
323	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
324	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
325	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
326	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
327	        return copy.deepcopy(record)
328	
329	    def _map_change_record(
330	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
331	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
332	        return {
333	            "type": "map_change",
334	            "tick": self.tick,
335	            "sequence": sequence,
336	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
337	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
338	        }
339	
340	    def _plan_route(
341	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
342	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
343	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
344	
345	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
346	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
347	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
348	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
349	        """
350	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
351	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)
352	
353	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
354	        for task in self.tasks.values():
355	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
356	                continue
357	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
358	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
359	                continue
360	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
361	            if route is None:
362	                robot.route = []
363	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
364	            else:
365	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
366	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
367	                robot.route = route
368	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
369	
370	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
371	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
372	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
373	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
374	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
375	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
376	                continue
377	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
378	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
379	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
380	                continue
381	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
382	            if route is None:
383	                robot.route = []
384	                continue
385	            robot.route = route
386	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
387	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

389	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
390	    # Traffic conflicts and yielding
391	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
392	
393	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
394	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
395	        cells: set[Position] = set()
396	        for robot in self.robots.values():
397	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
398	                cells.update(robot.route)
399	        return cells
400	
401	    def _safe_side_cells(
402	        self,
403	        robot: Robot,
404	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
405	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
406	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
407	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
408	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
409	
410	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
411	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
412	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
413	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
414	
415	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
416	          skips anything else),
417	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
418	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
419	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
420	          route is excluded), and
421	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
422	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
423	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
424	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
425	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
426	
427	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
428	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
429	        """
430	        blocked = set(forbidden)
431	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
432	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
433	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
434	                continue
435	            yield cell
436	
437	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
438	        self,
439	        blocker: Robot,
440	        requester: Robot,
441	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
442	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
443	    ) -> Position | None:
444	        """Free side-cell an idle blocker can yield to, or None.
445	
446	        The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would swap the
447	        two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is shared via
448	        :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one blockage for
449	        another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
450	        """
451	        return next(
452	            self._safe_side_cells(
453	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
454	            ),
455	            None,
456	        )
457	
458	    def _self_sidestep(
459	        self,
460	        robot: Robot,
461	        task: Task | None,
462	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
463	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
464	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
465	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
466	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
467	
468	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
469	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
470	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
471	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
472	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
473	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
474	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
475	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
476	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
477	        """
478	        if task is None or task.completed:
479	            return None
480	        destination = robot.route[0]
481	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
482	        if blocker_id is None:
483	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
484	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
485	        best_length = 0
486	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
487	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
488	        # that order as the tie break.
489	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
490	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
491	            if route is None:
492	                continue
493	            if (
494	                blocker_id is not None
495	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
496	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
497	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
498	                )
499	            ):
500	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
501	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
502	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
503	                continue
504	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
505	                best = (cell, route)
506	                best_length = len(route)
507	        return best
508	
509	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
510	        self,
511	        robot: Robot,
512	        side: Position,
513	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
514	        blocker_id: str,
515	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
516	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
517	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
518	    ) -> bool:
519	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
520	
521	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
522	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
523	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
524	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
525	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
526	        never rejected here.
527	        """
528	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
529	            return False
530	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
531	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
532	            return False
533	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
534	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
535	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
536	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
537	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
538	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
539	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
540	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
541	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
542	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
543	        return not self._can_vacate(
544	            blocker,
545	            robot,
546	            hyp_occupied,
547	            reserved,
548	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
549	            blocked_path,
550	        )
551	
552	    def _can_vacate(
553	        self,
554	        blocker: Robot,
555	        requester: Robot,
556	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
557	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
558	        checking: frozenset[str],
559	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
560	    ) -> bool:
561	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
562	
563	        An idle blocker leaves only by yielding onto a safe side cell for the
564	        requesting robot; a busy blocker leaves by driving onto its next
565	        waypoint (possibly following a chain of robots that all move this tick)
566	        or by sidestepping onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by
567	        map unreachability never move. *checking* names robots whose leave
568	        check is already on the call stack, so a cyclic dependency (a head-on
569	        deadlock, or the requester itself) is not assumed resolvable.
570	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive back
571	        through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so such
572	        sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on the
573	        blocker's own route does).
574	        """
575	        if blocker.robot_id in checking:
576	            return False
577	        task = self.tasks[blocker.task_id] if blocker.task_id is not None else None
578	        if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
579	            return False
580	        if task is not None and not blocker.route:
581	            # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this tick;
582	            # it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
583	            return False
584	        if task is None:
585	            # Idle robots only ever move by yielding for a requester, and they
586	            # do so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
587	            # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
588	            # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
589	            # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
590	            side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, requester, occupied, reserved)
591	            return side is not None and side not in blocked_path
592	        if blocker.route:
593	            ahead = blocker.route[0]
594	            if (
595	                self.grid.traversable(ahead)
596	                and ahead not in occupied
597	                and ahead not in reserved
598	            ):
599	                return True
600	            occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
601	            if (
602	                occupant_id is not None
603	                and occupant_id != blocker.robot_id
604	                and occupant_id not in checking
605	            ):
606	                # The blocker could follow the robot ahead once that robot
607	                # vacates its cell this same tick.
608	                if self._can_vacate(
609	                    self.robots[occupant_id],
610	                    requester,
611	                    occupied,
612	                    reserved,
613	                    checking | {blocker.robot_id},
614	                    blocked_path,
615	                ):
616	                    return True
617	        # Otherwise the blocker might sidestep onto a free side cell itself,
618	        # but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has to use --
619	        # parking there only moves the blockage.
620	        for side_cell in self._safe_side_cells(
621	            blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=blocked_path
622	        ):
623	            if self._plan_route(blocker, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
624	                return True
625	        return False
626	
627	    def _update_traffic_waits(
628	        self,
629	        waited: dict[str, str],
630	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
631	    ) -> None:
632	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
633	
634	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
635	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
636	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
637	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
638	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
639	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
640	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
641	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
642	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
643	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
644	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
645	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
646	        """
647	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
648	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
649	        for robot_id in waited:
650	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
651	                continue
652	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
653	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
654	                continue
655	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
656	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
657	                continue
658	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
659	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
660	                continue
661	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
662	            if entry is None:
663	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
664	            else:
665	                surviving[robot_id] = {
666	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
667	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
668	                }
669	        self._traffic_waits = surviving
670	
671	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
672	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
673	
674	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
675	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
676	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
677	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
678	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
679	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
680	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
681	        """
682	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
683	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
684	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
685	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
686	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
687	                continue
688	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
689	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
690	
691	    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
692	        return [
693	            {
694	                "robot_id": robot_id,
695	                "blocked_by": list(entry["blocked_by"]),
696	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
697	            }
698	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
699	        ]

702	    # Normal execution
703	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
704	
705	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
706	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest idle robot using stable tie breaks."""
707	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
708	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
709	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
710	            for robot in self.robots.values():
711	                if not robot.idle:
712	                    continue
713	                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
714	                if route is None:
715	                    continue
716	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
717	            if not choices:
718	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
719	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
720	                continue
721	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
722	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
723	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
724	            robot.route = route
725	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id
726	
727	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
728	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
729	        for robot in self.robots.values():
730	            if robot.task_id is None:
731	                continue
732	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
733	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
734	                task.picked_up = True
735	
736	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
737	        self._confirm_pickups()
738	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
739	        self.assign_tasks()
740	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
741	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
742	        self._confirm_pickups()
743	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
744	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
745	        moved: list[str] = []
746	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
747	        blocked_by: dict[str, str] = {}
748	
749	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
750	            del occupied[robot.position]
751	            robot.position = destination
752	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
753	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
754	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
755	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
756	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
757	
758	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
759	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
760	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
761	                continue
762	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
763	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
764	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
765	                continue
766	            if not robot.route:
767	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
768	                continue
769	            destination = robot.route[0]
770	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
771	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
772	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
773	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
774	                    if route is None:
775	                        robot.route = []
776	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
777	                    else:
778	                        robot.route = route
779	                continue
780	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
781	            if blocker_id is None:
782	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
783	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
784	                relocate(robot, destination)
785	                robot.route.pop(0)
786	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
787	                continue
788	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
789	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
790	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
791	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids:
792	                if blocker.task_id is None:
793	                    # Idle blocker: ask it to yield onto a free side cell,
794	                    # then take over the cell it vacated.
795	                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
796	                    if side is not None:
797	                        relocate(blocker, side)
798	                        relocate(robot, destination)
799	                        robot.route.pop(0)
800	                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
801	                        continue
802	                elif blocker.route:
803	                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
804	                    if (
805	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
806	                        and ahead not in occupied
807	                        and ahead not in reserved
808	                    ):
809	                        # The blocker is expected to drive on within this
810	                        # tick, so waiting one tick is cheaper than detouring.
811	                        blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
812	                        continue
813	            # The blocker cannot or will not move this tick: try to sidestep
814	            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
815	            side = self._self_sidestep(
816	                robot, task, occupied, reserved, frozenset(moved_ids)
817	            )
818	            if side is not None:
819	                cell, route = side
820	                relocate(robot, cell)
821	                robot.route = route
822	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
823	                continue
824	            blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
825	        self._update_traffic_waits(blocked_by, frozenset(moved_ids))
826	        self.tick += 1
827	        event: dict[str, object] = {
828	            "type": "tick",
829	            "tick": self.tick,
830	            "moved": moved,
831	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
832	            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),
833	        }
834	        self.replay.append(event)
835	        return event
836	
837	    def _finish_if_arrived(self, robot: Robot) -> None:
838	        if robot.task_id is None:
839	            return
840	        task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
841	        if task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
842	            return
843	        if robot.position == task.pickup:
844	            task.picked_up = True
845	        if task.picked_up and robot.position == task.dropoff and not robot.route:
846	            task.completed = True
847	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
848	            robot.task_id = None
849

851	        completed = sum(task.completed for task in self.tasks.values())
852	        return {
853	            "ticks": self.tick,
854	            "tasks_total": len(self.tasks),
855	            "tasks_completed": completed,
856	            "tasks_paused": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
857	            "completion_ratio": completed / len(self.tasks) if self.tasks else 1.0,
858	            "distance_total": sum(robot.distance_travelled for robot in self.robots.values()),
859	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
860	        }

890	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
891	        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.
892	
893	        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
894	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
895	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
896	        raise :class:`OSError`.
897	        """
898	        document = {
899	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
900	            "grid": {
901	                "width": self.grid.width,
902	                "height": self.grid.height,
903	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
904	            },
905	            "base_grid": {
906	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
907	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
908	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
909	            },
910	            "tick": self.tick,
911	            "robots": [
912	                {
913	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
914	                    "position": list(robot.position),
915	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
916	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
917	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
918	                }

992	    @classmethod

1024	        robots: list[Robot] = []

1027	            if not grid.traversable(position):
1028	                raise ValueError(
1029	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
1030	                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
1031	                )
1032	            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
1033	            previous = position
1034	            for index, cell in enumerate(record["route"]):
1035	                waypoint = _as_pair(
1036	                    cell, f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {index}"
1037	                )
1038	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
1039	                    raise ValueError(
1040	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
1041	                        "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
1042	                    )

1047	                    )

1052	                raise ValueError(

1054	                    "non-negative integer"
1055	                )

1057

1061	            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
1062	            tasks.append(
1063	                Task(
1064	                    record["task_id"],
1065	                    pickup,
1066	                    dropoff,

1068	                    record["picked_up"],
1069	                    record["completed"],
1070	                )
1071	            )
1072

1074	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
1075	
1076	        for robot in robots:

1078	                task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
1079	                if task is None:
1080	                    raise ValueError(
1081	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task {robot.task_id!r}"
1082	                    )
1083	                if task.completed:
1084	                    raise ValueError(
1085	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} that is "
1086	                        "already completed"
1087	                    )
1088	                if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:

1096	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:

1099	                )

1102	            # still in progress.
1103	            if not task.completed and task.assigned_robot is not None:
1104	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
1105	                if owner is None:
1106	                    raise ValueError(
1107	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
1108	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
1109	                    )
1110	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
1111	                    raise ValueError(
1112	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} but the "

1117	        cls._validate_active_task_routes(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id)
1118	        traffic_waits = cls._load_traffic_waits(data, robot_by_id)

1124	        simulator = cls(grid, robots, tasks)
1125	        simulator.base_grid = base_grid

1127	        simulator.replay = copy.deepcopy(replay)

1286	    @classmethod
1287	    def _load_map_changes(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
1288	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "map_changes")
1289	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
1290	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'map_changes' must be a list")
1291	        changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1292	        last_tick = -1
1293	        last_sequence = 0
1294	        for index, frame in enumerate(raw):
1295	            context = f"map change {index}"
1296	            if not isinstance(frame, dict):
1297	                raise ValueError(f"{context} must be an object")
1298	            tick = frame.get("tick")
1299	            sequence = frame.get("sequence")
1300	            if not _is_int(tick) or tick < 0:
1301	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'tick' must be a non-negative integer")
1302	            if not _is_int(sequence) or sequence <= 0:
1303	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'sequence' must be a positive integer")
1304	            if sequence != index + 1:
1305	                raise ValueError(
1306	                    f"map change sequences must run consecutively from 1; change {index} "
1307	                    f"has sequence {sequence}, expected {index + 1}"
1308	                )
1309	            if tick < last_tick:
1310	                raise ValueError(
1311	                    f"{context} tick {tick} is earlier than a preceding map change"
1312	                )
1313	            if tick == last_tick and sequence != last_sequence + 1:
1314	                raise ValueError(f"{context} breaks consecutive sequencing at tick {tick}")
1315	            added = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("added"), context, "added")
1316	            removed = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("removed"), context, "removed")
1317	            if not added and not removed:
1318	                raise ValueError(f"{context} contains no actual obstacle changes")
1319	            overlap = set(added) & set(removed)
1320	            if overlap:
1321	                cell = sorted(overlap)[0]
1322	                raise ValueError(
1323	                    f"{context} adds and removes the same cell {list(cell)}"
1324	                )
1325	            changes.append(
1326	                {
1327	                    "type": "map_change",
1328	                    "tick": tick,
1329	                    "sequence": sequence,
1330	                    "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
1331	                    "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
1332	                }
1333	            )
1334	            last_tick = tick
1335	            last_sequence = sequence
1336	        return changes

1338	    @classmethod
1339	    def _validate_map_history(
1340	        cls,
1341	        base_grid: GridMap,
1342	        saved_grid: GridMap,
1343	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
1344	    ) -> None:
1345	        obstacles = set(base_grid.obstacles)
1346	        width, height = saved_grid.width, saved_grid.height
1347	        for frame in changes:
1348	            for key in ("added", "removed"):
1349	                for cell in frame[key]:
1350	                    x, y = cell
1351	                    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
1352	                        raise ValueError(
1353	                            f"map change {frame['sequence']} cell {list(cell)} lies "
1354	                            "outside the map"
1355	                        )
1356	            added = {tuple(cell) for cell in frame["added"]}
1357	            removed = {tuple(cell) for cell in frame["removed"]}
1358	            for cell in added:
1359	                if cell in obstacles:
1360	                    raise ValueError(
1361	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} adds obstacle {list(cell)} "
1362	                        "that is already present according to the history"
1363	                    )
1364	            for cell in removed:
1365	                if cell not in obstacles:
1366	                    raise ValueError(
1367	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} removes obstacle {list(cell)} "
1368	                        "that is absent according to the history"
1369	                    )
1370	            obstacles |= added
1371	            obstacles -= removed
1372	        if obstacles != set(saved_grid.obstacles):
1373	            raise ValueError(
1374	                "the map reproduced from 'map_changes' does not match the saved grid"
1375	            )
